solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restrain pointer, very loud, circling copper

indicators.note: the pointer and the very loud marking go round the copper symbol, enclosing it

parts.note: a clock's hand is its pointer
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An order to hold back a pointer dog, loudly, while it circles a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, fitting the restraint picture, but here it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: To put cuffs on someone is to restrain them by the wrists, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: I must get led astray, disliking work

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of the word led are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being led astray because they dislike working.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who shuns labour is described as idle, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Small enough specimen

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ample means plenty or enough

explanation.surface: A specimen that is small but still big enough to test.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a portion taken as a representative specimen, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Saint Arnold, for example

definitions.meaning: St ... founded the Benedictine order of monks
... Arnold was the American general who betrayed his side to the British, so he bears this first name

explanation.surface: A description of a holy man named Arnold, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Benedict Arnold is the notorious Revolutionary War traitor, which makes 'Saint Arnold' a deliberately ironic pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the monastic saint; the other is the given name of the traitor Arnold.

clue.text: Energetic, a lively relative

indicators.note: lively suggests jumping about, so the letters of energetic and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a bouncy, energetic family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energetic' and 'lively' look like a pair of descriptions of the relative, but the first is fodder and the second the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a kind of family relative, the answer being a specific example.

clue.text: Strikes, with journalists

parts.note: hacks is slang for journalists

explanation.surface: Industrial action called alongside newspaper reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' reads as walkouts by workers, but the definition means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard blows or smacks are called whacks, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Unfair arrangements made by inexperienced hands

parts.note: a raw recruit is an inexperienced one
in card games a hand that is dealt is a deal

explanation.surface: Bad bargains struck by novice workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like workers, but it means the hands dealt in cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a bad bargain or harsh treatment is idiomatically getting this.

clue.text: Cast off in southern Irish lake

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern or south
lough is the Irish word for a lake, like the Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Someone casts off a boat on a lake in the south of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' suggests launching a boat, but here it means shedding, as a snake sheds skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is said to slough its skin, meaning it sheds or discards it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Blue celestial body close to Mercury

parts.note: our planet is a celestial body

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, so the end of Mercury is taken

explanation.surface: A bluish planet sits near Mercury in the solar system.
explanation.walkthrough: The planetary surface misleads: 'Blue' means rude or crude, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are coarse and bawdy, and earthy humour is similarly crude, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Advantage gained by club once wicket's taken

indicators.note: once the wicket letter is taken away it no longer appears in the golf club

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket team gains an advantage after taking a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides a golf club; cricket supplies only the deleted letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a slight lead or superiority over rivals is having an edge, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Source of article dividing French region

indicators.note: the article splits the region's name into two parts by sitting inside it

parts.note: Provence is the region of south-eastern France
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Tracing the origin of a newspaper piece that has caused division in a part of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The origin or documented history of an object, especially artwork, is its source, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Chase funds university collected

indicators.note: the purse collects or gathers up the university letter inside it

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money or funds, as a prize purse

explanation.surface: A university chases money it has collected.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue someone is to chase after them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Try joining golf club, one throwing a ball

parts.note: to have a shot at something is to try it
a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: Someone tries joining a golf club, which involves hitting a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture suggests a ball being hit, but the athlete throws a heavy ball in field events.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who hurls the heavy metal ball in the field event is described, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Fluency, blessing in disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the letters of blessing appear in a new order

explanation.surface: Plays on the phrase a blessing in disguise, applied to being fluent.
explanation.walkthrough: The familiar idiom 'blessing in disguise' masks the anagram fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib speech is smooth and easy, so the quality is fluency, often with a hint of insincerity.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic, US poet on fourth of July

parts.note: Robert Frost was a celebrated American poet

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the word July is selected

explanation.surface: An American poet is cool about Independence Day celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth of July' reads as the US holiday, apt beside a US poet, but it means the word's fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A frosty reception is cold and unwelcoming, showing no enthusiasm, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Choose filling fare for bigwigs seated here?

indicators.note: the word for choose fills the middle of the word for fare

parts.note: the table one keeps is the food or fare one serves
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Selecting what to put on the menu for important guests at their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling fare' suggests a hearty meal; 'filling' is the container signal and 'fare' gives the table, as in keeping a good table.
explanation.definitionFit: At formal dinners the most important guests sit at the head table, so the definition describes its use.

clue.text: Capital of a country in Asia, then Siam

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words Asia, then Siam

explanation.surface: Reads like a geography question about Asian capitals, Siam being old Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Asian setting misleads: the capital is European, Greece's.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, so it is an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Scandinavian boy and girl, first to identify evil manipulator

parts.note: Sven is a common Scandinavian boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: the first letter of identify is taken

explanation.surface: A Nordic couple are the first to spot a scheming villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, whose name came to mean a sinister controller.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is used for anyone who exerts malign control over another person, as in the novel.

clue.text: Navy member, a lawyer

parts.note: an arm is a limb or member of the body
DA, district attorney, is an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A naval officer turns out to be a lawyer too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like someone in the navy, but it means a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, so it is a navy, as with the Spanish Armada of 1588.

clue.text: Knowing daily produces something that'll kill insect pests

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or sharp-witted
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: A shrewd newspaper, rolled up, can be used to swat bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY meaning knowing or streetwise is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky coated paper hung up to trap and kill flies is a device for killing insect pests.

clue.text: Left noose uncoiled, so relax!

indicators.note: something uncoiled has its shape undone, so the letters of noose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has escaped a hanging noose is told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a grip or rule is to relax it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Key batsman facing the first ball of the innings

definitions.meaning: a key that undoes a lock or tin is a device for opening things

definitions.text: batsman facing the first ball of the innings
definitions.meaning: in cricket the two batsmen who start the innings are its ...

explanation.surface: Describes an important cricketer who takes the first delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective, important, describing the batsman, but it is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a tool that opens things; the other is the cricket term for a batsman who starts the innings.

clue.text: Curious boy, very likely to succeed

parts.note: curious means strange or odd
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A strange lad who is tipped to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting term for a favourite whose chance of winning is better than evens, so success is likely.

clue.text: Nicaraguan guerrilla group smuggled goods

parts.note: the Contras were US-backed rebels fighting Nicaragua's government in the 1980s
a band is a group of people or musicians

explanation.surface: A rebel group in Central America runs smuggled supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods imported or exported illegally are known as contraband, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Wild party sees opera character losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the character's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Porgy is the title hero of Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: An opera singer loses his head at a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is an unrestrained, wild celebration, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Exposed old writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An elderly author has been unmasked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author but means the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left open is uncovered and exposed, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Live it up, taking in a show

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the word for live it up surrounds the letter a

parts.note: to revel is to party and live it up

explanation.surface: An invitation to party hard while going out to see a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a theatre outing, but it is the verb to display.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show or disclose it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: What Everest is, especially?

definitions.meaning: the world's highest mountain towers higher than every other peak
a phrase meaning most of all or particularly

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the phrase literally: Everest stands over every other mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest literally stands over every peak; figuratively the phrase means most importantly or particularly.
